standards.name: AsyncAPI
standards.scope: The published AsyncAPI 3.0 document describes outbound app-webhook channels for the currently emitted app.parked, app.woken, and usage_statement.finalized events, plus the authenticated workflow external-event injection channel at POST /v1/workflows/runs/{id}/events.
standards.limitations: Queue contracts, workflow lifecycle/audit events, and the remaining closed-vocabulary webhook events are not yet described; legacy JSON webhook delivery remains outside this CloudEvents contract.

standards.name: CloudEvents
standards.surface: outbound webhooks, triggers, and queued events
standards.scope: App webhook subscriptions can opt into CloudEvents 1.0 structured JSON delivery with the standard context attributes and an account_id extension.
standards.limitations: CloudEvents is currently outbound app-webhook delivery only; the internal event router, trigger ingestion, and binary-mode bindings remain future work. Legacy JSON delivery remains the default.

standards.name: Sigstore Cosign
standards.scope: Per-app trusted-publisher enforcement verifies Cosign signatures before an OCI deploy.
standards.limitations: Enforcement is opt-in per app and Gregale does not claim full Sigstore policy-controller compatibility.

standards.name: CycloneDX
standards.scope: Successful application builds can publish a CycloneDX JSON SBOM for retrieval.
standards.limitations: SBOM generation is best-effort; platform release bundles use SPDX 2.3 instead.

standards.name: General Data Protection Regulation
standards.scope: The repository contains a DPA template, sub-processor disclosures, and account export/deletion flows.
standards.limitations: This is a contractual and engineering alignment package, not a legal determination or regulatory certification.

standards.name: gRPC
standards.surface: customer app edge and daemon-to-daemon APIs
standards.scope: Customer apps may opt into native gRPC framing; internal services use protobuf over gRPC.
standards.limitations: Customer gRPC is plan-gated and follows the app listener/readiness contract.

standards.name: HTTP/1.1
standards.scope: The universal default protocol for deployed HTTP apps and the legacy bridge path.
standards.limitations: The app must expose a reachable listener on the configured port; protocol upgrades are policy-controlled.

standards.name: HTTP/2
standards.scope: Apps selecting http2 receive native HTTP/2 framing through the stream bridge.
standards.limitations: The customer-facing selector is limited to the closed app_protocol set; HTTP/3 is not available.

standards.name: HTTP/3
standards.scope: No QUIC listener or HTTP/3 app-protocol selector is currently exposed.
standards.limitations: Clients use the upstream edge and the supported HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 paths today.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 27001
standards.scope: The repository contains a draft Statement of Applicability and mapped control evidence.
standards.limitations: This is not an ISO 27001 certification or independent attestation.

standards.name: JSON Web Tokens
standards.surface: workload identity and edge auth rules
standards.scope: Gregale mints short-lived RS256 workload tokens and supports JWT edge policy rules.
standards.limitations: Gregale is not a general-purpose OAuth authorization server; issuer and audience policy remain operator-configured.

standards.name: Mutual TLS
standards.scope: Internal cross-node control-plane traffic can be authenticated with mTLS.
standards.limitations: Customer-to-app mTLS is not a general edge feature; public TLS terminates at the platform edge.

standards.name: OAuth 2.0
standards.surface: dashboard login, CLI pairing, and workload exchange
standards.scope: Google/GitHub sign-in and OIDC-backed deploy-token exchange use OAuth-shaped bearer flows.
standards.limitations: Gregale does not currently expose a complete standards-based authorization-server surface for customer tenants.

standards.name: OCI Distribution
standards.scope: Gregale pulls OCI images from registries and resolves immutable digests.
standards.limitations: Full Distribution 1.1 conformance and OCI referrer artifacts are not yet a published contract.

standards.name: OCI Image Format
standards.surface: source builds and prebuilt image deployments
standards.scope: Gregale accepts digest-pinned OCI image references and converts image layers into its guest rootfs model.
standards.limitations: The runtime contract remains a stateless app listener; OCI volumes and host mounts are not portable into a VM.

standards.name: OpenID Connect
standards.surface: external identity and CI deploy authentication
standards.scope: Gregale verifies issuer/audience/subject claims for the OIDC deploy exchange and supports OAuth identity providers.
standards.limitations: Tenant SSO, discovery-driven provider onboarding, and SCIM provisioning are not yet supported.

standards.name: OpenTelemetry OTLP
standards.scope: Apps and daemons can use OTLP/HTTP, and Gregale propagates W3C trace context across the runtime boundary.
standards.limitations: The customer contract is strongest for traces and logs; a full tenant-facing OTLP metrics pipeline is not yet promised.

standards.name: PostgreSQL connection contract
standards.surface: managed database bindings and application environment
standards.scope: Managed PostgreSQL bindings expose standard connection URL material to workloads.
standards.limitations: Managed PostgreSQL remains an internal capability and is not yet a generally available database service.

standards.name: Prometheus exposition format
standards.scope: Every daemon exposes Prometheus metrics for scrape-based operations and alerting.
standards.limitations: The platform's customer API is not a generic PromQL proxy; metric names and labels are Gregale-owned contracts.

standards.name: HTTP Problem Details
standards.surface: public REST API and CLI errors
standards.scope: API failures use application/problem+json with stable machine-readable codes and recovery documentation.
standards.limitations: Legacy RFC 7807 clients remain wire-compatible; RFC 9457 is the canonical successor. Gregale-specific code and extension members remain outside the base standard.

standards.name: security.txt
standards.scope: The repository publishes a machine-readable security contact policy at /.well-known/security.txt.
standards.limitations: The file advertises disclosure contacts; it does not itself provide vulnerability-management automation.

standards.name: HTTP Problem Details
standards.scope: Public JSON errors use the RFC 9457 problem-details envelope with application/problem+json, stable Gregale error codes and extensions, and support the standard occurrence URI when supplied.
standards.limitations: The contract is JSON-only and retains Gregale-specific code and extension members; XML serialization and registered common problem types are not claimed.

standards.name: Amazon S3 API
standards.surface: private object storage and signed URLs
standards.scope: The branded gateway supports common bucket, object, multipart, metadata, and signed-request operations.
standards.limitations: Compatibility is provider-qualified and intentionally scoped; Gregale does not claim every AWS S3 operation or semantic.

standards.name: Server-Sent Events
standards.surface: logs, events, execution, and build streams
standards.scope: Live logs and platform event streams use text/event-stream with reconnect cursors where applicable.
standards.limitations: SSE is a server-to-client stream; bidirectional realtime workloads use the managed realtime surface.

standards.name: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria
standards.surface: security, availability, confidentiality, and privacy controls
standards.scope: The repository contains a draft control mapping to code, policies, runbooks, and operational evidence.
standards.limitations: No independent SOC 2 examination or attestation has been completed.

standards.name: SPDX
standards.scope: Release tarballs carry SPDX 2.3 SBOMs and the installer gates CRITICAL/HIGH CVE regressions against a known-good baseline.
standards.limitations: The release parser is intentionally SPDX-only; application build SBOMs use CycloneDX.

standards.name: Transport Layer Security
standards.scope: The upstream public edge terminates customer TLS 1.3 and supports managed certificates for Gregale and custom domains.
standards.limitations: Certificate issuance is operator/edge-provider managed; customer client certificates are not a general edge feature.

standards.name: W3C Trace Context
standards.scope: Gregale accepts, validates, stamps, and forwards W3C trace context into customer runtimes.
standards.limitations: Guest-boundary baggage is size/member bounded to protect the VM and gateway hot path.

standards.name: WebSocket
standards.scope: The managed realtime service provides durable endpoint configuration for long-lived WebSocket clients.
standards.limitations: Ordinary scale-to-zero request apps are not promised as an unbounded WebSocket host; long-lived connections affect parking and placement.
